findings.claim: The test inputs '22.846685108', '20.123456789' and 25.5, when multiplied by 1e9, all produce exact integers, so BigInt() accepts them without needing Math.round; these tests do not actually exercise the fractional-value fix.
This second float test case has the same problem as the one at line 241: its inputs yield exact integer wei values, so it passes even without Math.round and does not verify the fix.
Because no test produces a fractional wei value, removing Math.round here would not cause any test to fail, leaving the new rounding behavior unprotected by tests.
Same as the line 64/65 issue: this second Math.round call is also not covered by a test that would fail if the rounding were removed.

Number(''), Number(' ') and Number(null) all evaluate to 0, which passes the Number.isFinite check, and negative numeric strings also pass; this lets an oracle response with an empty, null, or negative gas price value be treated as a valid, winning price instead of being rejected so the code falls through to the next oracle or fixed config.
The same missing positivity check exists at this second location, allowing zero, empty, null, or negative oracle values to be accepted as a valid gas price.
The tests replace global.fetch with a jest mock instead of using MSW, which deviates from the project's stated rule (AGENTS.md:374) to use MSW rather than mocking fetch directly.

Much of this new test suite duplicates cases already covered in apps/web/src/hooks/__tests__/useGasPrice.test.ts (first oracle, fallback to second oracle, fixed fallback, fixed 1559, speed-up), creating redundant test coverage across the two files.
The getTotalFee 'large values' test case is identical to the one in apps/web/src/hooks/__tests__/useGasPrice.test.ts:334-337, duplicating test logic instead of consolidating it.

The sequence of multiplying by gweiFactor, checking finiteness, rounding, and converting to BigInt is repeated three times in the file instead of being extracted into a shared helper, making it easy for a future fix (such as the positivity check) to be applied in only some of the places.
This is a second repetition of the same multiply/check/round/convert logic noted at lines 55-65, reinforcing the duplication issue.
